chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him, ‘May I perform sajdah upon tar, meaning upon bitumen?’ He said, ‘No, nor upon cloth made from cotton, nor upon wool, nor upon anything from an animal, nor upon food, nor upon anything from the fruits of the earth, nor upon anything from furnishings.’

key_terms.أَسْجُدُ: I perform sajdah; the act of prostrating in salat
key_terms.الرِّيَاشِ: furnishings or adornments; items used for comfort or decoration
key_terms.الزِّفْتِ: tar; a dark resinous substance used as a surface material
key_terms.الصُّوفِ: wool; a textile material from animals
key_terms.الْقِيرِ: bitumen or pitch; clarification of the intended substance
key_terms.الْكُرْسُفِ: cotton; here referring to cloth made from cotton
key_terms.ثِمَارِ الْأَرْضِ: fruits of the earth; edible produce grown from the land

ai.seo_question: On what materials is sajdah not permitted according to Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the validity of sajdah and specifies materials upon which sajdah is not to be performed. It prohibits sajdah on tar, cotton cloth, wool, animal-derived things, food items, fruits of the earth, and furnishings, reflecting the jurisprudential limits for the place of prostration.
